Photograph: Saul Loeb,dave Chan/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The US president, Donald Trump, and Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, have each blamed the opposite side for the breakdown in negotiations. Photograph: Saul Loeb,dave Chan/AFP/Getty Images Canada ‘No more!!!’: Trump lashes out after US-Canada talks devolve into trade war PM Mark Carney says ‘we got attacked’ as tariffs come into force on items from hockey sticks to tongue depressors Lauren Almeida Sun 23 Aug 2026 07.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 07.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump has hit back at Canada after a breakdown in negotiations plunged the two countries into a trade war . In his first public comments since negotiations collapsed on Friday in Washington, the US president wrote on social media: “Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!” “They have also charged our great farmers, for many years, massive amounts of tariffs,” he added. “No more!!!” His comments came after the US imposed 50% tariffs on $20bn (£14.6bn) worth of Canadian goods, while Mark Carney , the country’s prime minister, has vowed to match them “dollar for dollar”. The US tariffs came into force on Saturday, ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors. Trade experts have predicted that the tariffs could result in some job losses, but the biggest impact is expected to be political, triggering fresh tension between the neighbours. View image in fullscreen Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc, left, and US trade representative Jamieson Greer speak to reporters in Washington DC on Friday. Photograph: Canadian Press/Shutterstock Both sides blamed the other for the breakdown in talks on Friday. Carney told Canadian journalists that the country was “at war” over trade with the US, after Trump “miscalculated” by escalating his tariff attack. “You’re at war when you’re attacked, and we got attacked,” the Canadian prime minister told reporters in Ottawa. “We cannot accept what they’ve offered and we will not give what they’ve asked.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion Against the wind: despite Trump’s attacks, unions are fighting for good US clean energy jobs Read more Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, has said the US was compelled to act after a year of retaliatory measures by Canada. He told Fox & Friends Weekend: “We’ve said enough and so we’ve taken countermeasures. Our interest is in protecting American workers and protecting American supply chains.” Carney, who previously served as the governor of the Bank of England, was elected as Canada’s prime minister last year after campaigning to lead a fightback against Trump, who has previously suggested he wants to make Canada a 51st state with “economic force”. Carney’s “dollar for dollar” tariffs are expected to take effect from 8 September, with new levies on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics. The escalation has also called into question the future of the North American trade pact between the US, Canada and Mexico, known as USMCA. The pact, which was signed by Trump during his first term, governs about $2tn annually in goods and services between the three countries. Trump refused to renew the USMCA this summer after Canada and Mexico formally requested for it to be renewed for another 16 years. When asked how the US-Canadian collapse in trade talks would affect the USMCA, Carney said it was “certainly not good news”. "If we waver in Germany, then Europe wavers. If Europe wavers, then Ukraine wavers as well," he cautioned at the ceremony in Münster where the Westphalian Peace Prize was awarded to NATO . Merz specifically warned that Russia could attack Germany and NATO if Ukraine falls. "If we fail to stop Moscow, then sooner or later, the Russian war machine will turn against us, against NATO itself. We must not turn a blind eye to this danger," he stressed. The German chancellor emphasized that without German aid, the war against Ukraine would result in an "imposed peace." This would lead to mass migration toward the West and the destabilization of the Ukrainian state, according to Merz. He touched only briefly on the meeting between Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in New York last weekend. Merz said it was yet another example of how diplomatic efforts fell on deaf ears in Moscow. Russia understands only the “language of strength” and must be brought to the negotiating table through this approach, he stressed. Merz said that "unity and strength remain prerequisites for successful negotiations with Moscow. And this can only encourage us to keep the United States of America by our side in our policy regarding Ukraine." Merz calls for unity against AfD Merz said that a united front is also needed in Germany, where the far-right Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has seen significant success in recent state elections and currently leads in nationwide polls. "We in Germany, too, will not allow ourselves to be divided," Merz said. "Not by hybrid attacks, not by social media agitation driven by Moscow-controlled bots, and... not by the slogans of the AfD and its Russian backers." The AfD wants Berlin to stop providing military and financial support to Ukraine, lift sanctions against Russia, and restore dialogue. What is Westphalian Peace Prize? The Westphalian Peace Prize is awarded every two years by the Economic Society for Westphalia and Lippe (WWL). The award commemorates the Peace of Westphalia of 1648, which was concluded in the town halls of Münster and Osnabrück. It brought an end to the Thirty Years’ War and is regarded as a contribution to the European peace order among states with equal rights. In response to a parliamentary question by Left Party politician Clara Bünger, the Interior Ministry said 25 cases had been examined since the court ruling on July 22, but all had been rejected. After the Taliban retook power in Afghanistan in August 2021, the previous coalition government of Social Democrats (SPD) , Greens and Free Democrats (FDP) had promised to grant entry to Afghan nationals who had worked for German institutions there or who were seen as endangered. The current conservative-led government paused that program in May 2025 and in December 2025, the Interior Ministry rescinded all entry permissions that had been given under the scheme , saying there was "no political interest" in taking the people in. The Federal Constitutional Court however ruled in July that Germany could not revoke the scheme en masse and that admission requests had to be considered on a case-to-case basis. Bünger called on the government "to take in the some 500 people still in question immediately and in an uncomplicated manner." She said the fact that these Afghan nationals had been forced to live for years in fear and uncertainty was unjustifiable. https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/black-c.text: A 'copycat killer' who tried to mutilate a sex worker's body inside a creepy 'kill room' he set up inside a '£30-a-night' Airbnb in Oldbury has confessed to his horrific murder. Benjamin Day, from Redditch , was so obsessed with US television show Dexter that he rented a room in Tividale and transformed it to mimic the terrifying crimes committed by the show's fictional serial killer. The 20-year-old spent 'hours preparing' for his brutal killing of Maria Saceanu and 'copied things he had seen' in the drama - including trying to sever her limbs, putting plastic sheeting down and keeping a microscopic slide of her blood as a 'trophy'. He even 'changed into his Dexter clothing', a khaki T-Shirt with buttons halfway down, before she arrived at the property in Barncroft Road, Detectives later found a disturbing 'shopping list' on his mobile, drafted by Day a month earlier. It featured knives, scissors, a mask, an apron, disposable gloves, duct tape, a staple gun, cleaning chemicals, a pipette, duffle bag, latex gloves, number plates and 'Hefty bags' - what 'Americans use to describe heavy duty black bin bags'. The killer had 'planned to get away with it' but he was caught out when his 'meticulous' plan 'all went wrong' and he cut his own hand while trying to 'dismember' Ms Saceanu's body. Day then 'quite deliberately' walked 20 minutes away from the scene and dialled 999 for himself as his victim's naked body lay on the floor of the kill room, hoping to return and 'finish the job' once his 'nasty' wound was patched up. Day, of Yeadon Close, Redditch, Worcestershire , had denied murder between December 19 and 22 last year. But he changed his plea in a dramatic court U-turn on the second day of his trial at Wolverhampton Crown Court. His confession on Tuesday, October 6, came after the prosecution had opened the case and started lining out the evidence to the jury. READ MORE: 'Dexter copycat killer tried to mutilate woman's body in Oldbury Airbnb' - jury told Mr Justice Bryan KC told Day a pre-sentence report will now be prepared ahead of his sentencing in December. Jurors heard how the show follows character Dexter Morgan, a forensic scientist working in a police department who is a serial killer and 'knows how to' cover up what he has done. Prosecutor Rachel Brand KC said 'there is no dispute from the defence in this case that his fascination with that programme, Dexter, played a part in his actions leading up to the night that Ms Saceanu was killed'. It was anticipated that Day was to claim self-defence, insisting that he set up the room to film a 'tribute' to Dexter to post on TikTok. Ms Saceanu, who was from Romania, was contacted by Day shortly after 9.30pm on Saturday, December 20 last year. She had listed her details on a site called Vivastreet - a website which sex workers use to get in touch with potential clients. Ms Brand told the jury: "We don't suggest that this case is about sex. "There is no evidence, actually, that any sexual contact took place between Day and Ms Saceanu on the night that she was killed. "The fact is, because she was a sex worker, she was available. "She was a person who could be hired and therefore lured to a particular place with the pretext that she was going to meet a client." The victim was captured on CCTV when she arrived about 50 minutes later in her car - a recording the prosecution said was the 'last time she was seen alive'. Day, who was 19 at the time and living with his parents, was inside the double bedroom he had rented from about 5.30pm, 'preparing'. He then killed her 'within a very short time of her arrival'. READ MORE: Secret to getting the best of BirminghamLive's stories After his killing, Day cut off Ms Saceanu's clothes with scissors and removed her jewellery before dumping them into a bin bag 'ready for disposal'. University of Worcester student Day injured himself as he tried to dismember Ms Saceanu's body and 'bound up his own hand with gaffer tape'. He was captured on CCTV leaving the Airbnb at 12.30am on Sunday, December 21, and walked 'some distance' before calling the emergency services about 20 minutes later. At 1.05am, Day texted the Airbnb landlord and asked if he could extend his stay to one week, or at least two or three days, before the police arrived about five minutes later. Ms Brand told the jury: "He said that the injury to his hand had been caused when he had been bitten by a fox or a wild dog. "The police found that explanation to be curious and it was also curious that he had bound up his own hand with gaffer tape." Day was taken to Russells Hall Hospital by paramedics and was arrested there at 3.42am on Saturday, December 21. Ms Saceanu suffered 78 wounds, caused by knives, many of which are said to have been inflicted after she was dead. It is thought she died 'as a result of wounds to her neck' which damaged her carotid artery or jugular vein. Ms Brand said: "However, despite such wounds, she may not have collapsed immediately and it's significant that there were a number of wounds to her hands which were consistent with efforts to protect herself, to defend herself." There were 'attempts to dismember her body', demonstrated by injuries including those to her elbow, wrist and knee, the court heard. In a statement read to the court, the landlord of the Airbnb said the property had three rooms for rent - two double rooms and a single room. The normal rate was £30 for a single guest and an additional £10 for an extra guest. Through Airbnb, Day booked for two guests and paid £40 - plus commission and vat, which came to a total of £46.78.
